title: What Happens If You Hold Your Breath Too Long?
description:
Send this to the friend who swears the urge to breathe means you're out of oxygen.
The urge to breathe is driven mainly by carbon dioxide building up, not by oxygen running low: sensors near your brainstem pick up the acid CO2 makes, and your diaphragm starts moving on its own. Oxygen only drives breathing hard when it gets very low, which is why breath-holding in water is dangerous: you can black out without any warning (also called shallow water or hypoxic blackout). The CDC warns that underwater breath-holding games can kill even strong swimmers. Never play them. Questions about your breathing? See a doctor.
